title: Machine learning pioneer Michael I. Jordan dismantles AI doom rhetoric as "grand moralizing performance"
key_facts: Michael I. Jordan, professor emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley, now works full time at Inria, the French research institute in Paris, where he heads a new 'markets and learning' chair; he spoke to the French newspaper Libération.
He called this summer's AI discourse 'totally frustrating' and called warnings of existential AI threats science fiction; 'superintelligence' is 'a science-fiction term'.
He called AI companies' demands for regulation 'theater' and said they 'would like to have total control over how they are regulated'.
He called the resignation of Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, which sparked a wave of fear in early September, 'a textbook example' of 'a grand moralizing performance'.
He said of Geoffrey Hinton's argument for superintelligence: 'None of the steps in this argument is credible'; he was 'a little different' on Yoshua Bengio, who focuses on safety.
He called the hack of Hugging Face by OpenAI agents bad engineering and said OpenAI was 'conducting rather stupid experiments'.
He called the data-centre investments 'just an enormous bet, but we have absolutely no idea whether it will pay off'.
quote_evidence: Jordan sees the whole thing as 'a grand moralizing performance that doesn't serve the real objective it claims to pursue.'
Jordan considers the massive data center investments 'just an enormous bet, but we have absolutely no idea whether it will pay off.'
why_it_matters_hint: A leading machine-learning researcher publicly disputes the doom arguments of other prominent scientists, in the middle of a heated safety debate.
event_date: The Decoder article 13 Oct 2026; date of the Libération interview not stated.
notes: Full text read from fulltext/C05-14.txt. The Libération original was not opened; the Decoder's summary of it is the source read. Our 6 Oct 2026 edition carried the AP on Coxon's testimony; our 30 Sep 2026 edition carried WIRED on the Hugging Face lawsuit; our 5 and 11 Oct editions carried Hinton's criticism of Trump.
